source.title: Affinity and Diversity: Quantifying Mechanisms of Data Augmentation
source.authors: Raphael Gontijo-Lopes; S. Smullin; E. Cubuk; Ethan Dyer

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether turning off data augmentation affects generalization on true labels, a component of V5, using augmentation schedule comparisons. It does not test fitting random labels.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own augmentation and switch-off results on true-label CIFAR-10 and ImageNet. It does not measure fitting random labels, shuffled pixels, or noisy-label learning. Cited random-label results are not this paper's results.
record.test_reason: The study tests the true-label generalization component of V5 through clean-training controls and experiments switching off augmentation or weight decay. It does not test random-label fitting.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: Affinity and Diversity jointly characterize augmentation performance, increased effective training-set size is necessary for beneficial augmentation in these experiments, and appropriately timed removal of regularization can improve performance.
record.recipe_differences: Studies augmentation policies and switch-off schedules on true labels rather than random-label fitting; evaluates WRN-28-2 on CIFAR-10 and ResNet-50 on ImageNet.
record.method_sensitivity: The effect varies by augmentation and switch-off timing; the paper notes FlipUD(100%) can be harmful when used throughout but beneficial when used only for the first third of training. Static and dynamic augmentation also differ.

fits_no_version.finding: Static augmentation generally underperforms clean training and performs worse than corresponding stochastic dynamic augmentation; crop gains are smaller than the standard error.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Beneficial augmentation depends on increasing the effective number of training examples, alongside distributional compatibility.

record.problems: ImageNet experiments use one initialization and have no error statistics. The reported switch-off result for FlipUD(100%) has no exact accuracy in the text. Static-augmentation comparisons are mostly described in aggregate; crop gains are explicitly smaller than the standard error on the mean.
record.rows_left_out: Other augmentation switch-off and static/dynamic results are summarized but not separately recorded; the text does not provide individual result values for them. See Sections 4.2–4.3 and Figures 5–6.

untested.parts: All parts: completely random labels, near-zero training error, chance test performance, and unchanged training settings.
All parts: relative fitting time for random labels and convergence across label-corruption fractions.
All parts. Adding Gaussian noise to real images does not test memorizing pure Gaussian-noise inputs.
All parts: perfect training fits and test-error trajectories across random-label corruption fractions.

Whether explicit regularization prevents fitting random labels; dropout removal; removal of augmentation and weight decay together; and whether removing weight decay from the outset preserves generalization. Switch-off experiments retain regularization during early training.
All parts: learning shared real-data patterns before memorizing noisy or random labels.

missing.what: Own experiment comparing constant weight decay with weight decay switched off partway through training, showing a validation-accuracy boost. Record the schedule and readable outcome separately.
missing.locator: Section 4.2; Figure 5(a), middle panel and caption

missing.what: Standalone true-label clean-training control: WRN-28-2 achieves 89.7 ± 0.1% CIFAR-10 test accuracy without augmentation, with weight decay 0.0005 retained.

record.verdict_notes: No evidence challenges V5 here. Benefits of particular augmentation policies do not contradict the claim that good generalization can occur without augmentation. Switch-off schedules were selected using validation accuracy on CIFAR-10 and test accuracy on ImageNet.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting, test error at chance, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Training time and convergence as label corruption increases.
Fitting shuffled-pixel, permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Training and test error across corruption fractions.

Whether augmentation, weight decay, or dropout prevent fitting random labels; whether removing weight decay or dropout affects true-label generalization. The study evaluates switch-off of augmentation on true labels.
Whether real-label patterns are learned before noisy or random labels.

rows.subject: WRN-28-2
rows.operation_detail: Trained with FlipUD(100%) only for the first third, then switched to clean data; compared final test accuracy with the clean baseline.

conditions.value: augmentation used for only the first third of training

rows.measure: Final test accuracy relative to the clean baseline
rows.value: final test accuracy is above the baseline
rows.note: The paper does not state the exact accuracy for this switch-off condition in the text.
rows.check: Supports only removing augmentation after early training: final accuracy exceeds the 89.7 ± 0.1% clean baseline. Weight decay remains enabled; this does not establish that all explicit regularization is unnecessary.

source_check.locator_found: Section 3; Section 4.2, Figure 5(b) and accompanying text; Appendix A.

rows.subject: WRN-28-2
rows.operation_detail: Compared static augmentation with clean training and dynamic augmentation across tested transforms.

conditions.value: almost all tested static augmentations; crop variants are exceptions noted by the authors

rows.measure: Test accuracy relative to the clean baseline and dynamic counterpart
rows.value: static augmentation yields lower test accuracy than the clean baseline for almost all tested augmentations; crop gains are less than the standard error on the mean; static augmentations always perform worse than their dynamic counterparts
rows.uncertainty: crop differences are less than the standard error on the mean
rows.note: Aggregate statements over tested augmentations; no individual transform values are given in the prose.
rows.check: The static-versus-dynamic augmentation result measures augmentation design and effective dataset size. Its poorer static performance does not establish a limitation of V5. Deterministic transforms are excluded from the dynamic superiority comparison because their static and dynamic cases coincide.

rows.subject: WRN-28-2
rows.operation_detail: Switched FlipUD(100%) off after the first third of training and continued with clean data.

conditions.value: augmentation used for only the first third of training

rows.measure: Final test accuracy compared with training with FlipUD(100%) throughout
rows.baseline: without switching, FlipUD(100%) decreases test accuracy by almost 50% compared to clean baseline
rows.value: final test accuracy is above the clean baseline
rows.note: The text gives no exact switch-off test accuracy.
rows.check: Duplicates R1's switch-off experiment with a different comparator; do not count as independent evidence. The nearly 50% accuracy decrease describes continuous FlipUD training, not the switch-off condition.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-10, WRN-28-2, FlipUD(100%) removed after the first third of training
relationships.reason: Final test accuracy exceeds the clean baseline after augmentation is removed, supporting the true-label removal component in this schedule (R1, R3; one experiment).
relationships.display_finding: Final test accuracy exceeded the clean baseline after vertical-flip augmentation was removed following the first third of training.
